data.product: Northbeam gives operations teams one view of every load, exception and handoff across terminals. It shows each load past its ETA window with the reason and the next action, keeps one timeline per load from pickup to proof of delivery, and shows lane volumes, dwell times and dispatcher workload in one view. It reads from the customer's TMS and writes nothing back unless asked. A rollout takes ten weeks: connect in weeks 1 and 2, pilot at one site in weeks 3 to 6, then every site in weeks 7 to 10. Pricing is shared on the call.

data.rollout_lead: Ten weeks from the first connection to all seven terminals, with Joliet as the pilot site because that is where the new volume and the open roles are.

rollout.title: Connect
rollout.body: We connect your TMS and the Joliet dispatch board. Your security review runs alongside. Nothing changes for dispatchers yet.

rollout.title: Pilot at Joliet
rollout.body: Joliet's dispatchers run the exception board for 30 days with a weekly check-in. We compare late-load calls against September.

rollout.title: All seven terminals
rollout.body: Two terminals a week, with the Joliet team training the next site. You get the capacity view across all lanes at the end.

faq.a: No. It reads from it. Dispatchers keep the TMS for planning and use Northbeam for exceptions and handoffs. Nothing is written back unless you ask for it.

faq.q: How long does the first connection take?
faq.a: The first two weeks of a rollout are for connecting the TMS and one dispatch board. Dispatchers change nothing in that time.
We share pricing on the call, so you see the numbers next to the pilot plan.

faq.q: How much time does it take from the dispatch team?
faq.a: That depends on the setup, and we go through it on the call. The pilot site's dispatchers are the ones who use the board day to day.
